topicName: Compute Engine: Load Balancing (HTTP(S), TCP, Internal)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Compute Engine: Load Balancing (HTTP(S), TCP, Internal)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Google Cloud's Compute Engine offers a variety of load balancing options to distribute traffic across multiple virtual machine (VM) instances. This ensures high availability, scalability, and fault tolerance for your applications. This tutorial covers HTTP(S), TCP, and Internal load balancing."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"HTTP(S) Load Balancing"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"HTTP(S) load balancing distributes HTTP and HTTPS traffic to backend instances. It operates at the application layer (Layer 7) and can make routing decisions based on request attributes like URL, headers, and cookies. This allows for advanced features like content-based routing and session affinity."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Global HTTP(S) Load Balancing: Distributes traffic across multiple regions, providing high availability and low latency for users worldwide."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Regional HTTP(S) Load Balancing: Distributes traffic within a single region, offering lower latency and cost compared to global load balancing."},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"To configure HTTP(S) load balancing, you'll typically need to create the following resources:"},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Backend services: Define the backend instances or instance groups that will receive traffic."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"URL maps: Define how incoming requests are routed to different backend services based on URL paths or hostnames."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Target proxies: Receive requests from the load balancer and forward them to the appropriate backend service based on the URL map."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Forwarding rules: Define the IP address and port that the load balancer listens on and forward traffic to the target proxy."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"# Example gcloud command to create a backend service
gcloud compute backend-services create my-backend-service \
    --global \
    --protocol HTTP \
    --health-checks my-health-check"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"TCP Load Balancing"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"TCP load balancing distributes TCP traffic to backend instances. It operates at the transport layer (Layer 4) and provides basic load balancing functionality. It's suitable for applications that don't require application-layer routing."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Global TCP Load Balancing: Distributes TCP traffic across multiple regions."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Regional TCP Load Balancing: Distributes TCP traffic within a single region."},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"The configuration process is similar to HTTP(S) load balancing, but uses TCP-specific resources."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"# Example gcloud command to create a TCP load balancer
gcloud compute forwarding-rules create my-tcp-forwarding-rule \
    --global \
    --ip-protocol TCP \
    --ports 80,443 \
    --target-pool my-target-pool"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Internal Load Balancing"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Internal load balancing distributes traffic to backend instances within the same Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) network. It's used for internal applications that don't need to be exposed to the public internet. It supports both TCP and HTTP(S) traffic."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Internal HTTP(S) Load Balancing: Distributes HTTP(S) traffic within a VPC network."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Internal TCP Load Balancing: Distributes TCP traffic within a VPC network."},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"Internal load balancing uses a private IP address within your VPC network. This allows internal services to communicate with each other without exposing them to the internet."},{"order":24,"type":"code","text":"# Example gcloud command to create an internal HTTP(S) load balancer
gcloud compute forwarding-rules create my-internal-forwarding-rule \
    --region us-central1 \
    --ip-protocol TCP \
    --ports 80 \
    --target-http-proxy my-internal-http-proxy \
    --address 10.10.10.10 \
    --subnet my-subnet"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"When configuring internal load balancing, ensure that the health checks are configured correctly to monitor the health of the backend instances. Also, verify that firewall rules allow traffic between the load balancer and the backend instances."},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"Choosing the right load balancing option depends on your application's requirements. Consider factors like traffic type (HTTP(S) or TCP), geographic distribution, and internal vs. external access when making your decision."}]
